name: Best Returner (point-in-time)
description: At each year-end close, buy the point-in-time S&P 500 constituent with the best total return over the calendar year just ended, and hold that single name until the next year-end close.

data_source.label: Yahoo Finance free daily prices
data_source.banner: POINT-IN-TIME ATTEMPT — free prices. Membership is the fja05680/sp500 history from 1996, not a survivorship-bias-free CRSP tape. Names Yahoo and Stooq cannot price are logged. Prior-year returns above +1000% are dropped unless a second vendor confirms them. Sharadar (SEP / SF1 / TICKERS) is the exact source.

universe.note: Membership is the fja05680/sp500 snapshot file (S&P 500 Historical Components & Changes), last row carried forward with Wikipedia changes after that file ends. Wikipedia's selected-changes table supplies bankruptcy notes and ticker continuations. That table records 411 changes (62 of them before 2011) and is not a complete delisting tape. A prior-year return above +1000% is dropped unless a second vendor confirms it. Sharadar TICKERS is the complete membership file.
universe.description: At each year-end close, buy the point-in-time S&P 500 constituent with the best total return over the calendar year just ended, and hold that single name until the next year-end close.

caveats: SURVIVORSHIP-BIASED — free Yahoo Finance source. The universe is the current S&P 500, not point-in-time membership. A survivorship-bias-free universe requires Sharadar (SEP / SF1 / TICKERS).
Prices are Yahoo's daily bars. Adjusted closes (Adj Close) include splits and dividends. Traded closes (Close) are split-adjusted only and are what the market-cap approximation multiplies by shares.

Historical market cap ≈ nearest reported shares × later splits × split-adjusted close. If Yahoo has no share history, today's share count is used instead. This is not point-in-time. Sharadar SF1 marketcap replaces it.
Rebalance is the year-end close. The signal uses only prices through that close. The fill is that same close, which is a small optimistic bias versus trading the next open.
Equal weight. Dividends enter through adjusted closes: the book holds a constant share count of the adjusted series, which matches total return.

Market caps printed on the holdings are the free-data approximation and are not used to select names. Historical market cap on the free source is an approximation: split-adjusted close × the nearest Yahoo share count, multiplied by splits that occurred after that share-count date. Dates before Yahoo's first share record use the earliest record. Names with no share history use today's share count. Buybacks, issuance, and stale records are not corrected. Sharadar SF1 marketcap replaces this.
warnings: Stooq answered with a browser check instead of a CSV, so it filled no delisted names on this run. Unpriceable tickers are listed on the book.
18 removed tickers had no Yahoo/Stooq prints during a membership spell (often a recycled symbol, or a delisted name Yahoo no longer stores): ADT, APC, BBBY, CAM, CSRA, EMC, INFO, NE, …

metrics.sharpe_basis: annualized daily simple returns, rf=0, 252-day year

benchmark.name: S&P 500 (SPY)
benchmark.note: SPY adjusted close (total return), rebased to this book's starting capital on the book's first date. Reference only.

metrics.sharpe_basis: annualized daily simple returns, rf=0, 252-day year

robustness.note: Hole-weighted bound. Fraction f of members had no usable signal-year return. Worst replaces that fraction with -100% for the holding year. Neutral replaces it with SPY's return over the same holding window. Excluded is the published book, which skips unpriceable names. This does not mean the missing name was the winner.
